question.text: Mr. Sharma, a retired postal officer with 15 years of service, has obtained his Series V-B certification. A client asks him to help invest in a sectoral/thematic fund (for example, a pharma sector fund). What should Mr. Sharma do?

answer.text: Politely decline and explain that sectoral/thematic funds fall outside the simple-and-performing scheme range permitted to a new cadre distributor
Go ahead and sell the sectoral/thematic fund since he has a valid certification
Sell it but inform the AMC later
Sell it as a one-time exception

explanation.text: The Logic: New cadre distributors with Series V-B certification are permitted to sell only simple and performing schemes — broadly Liquid/Money Market, Index, Diversified Equity, Retirement Benefit, and FMPs. Sectoral/thematic funds are concentrated, non-diversified products and are outside this simple-and-performing permitted range. The correct action is to decline and refer the client to a Series V-A distributor. The Trap: Holding a valid certification does not authorise selling every scheme. Series V-B has a deliberately narrow permitted product scope, and concentrated sector/thematic funds are excluded. Note: Whenever a scheme does not clearly fall within the simple-and-performing permitted list, decline and refer to a Series V-A distributor — selling outside the authorised product range can expose the distributor to regulatory action and ARN risk.
